definition_zh: 听；倾听；听从；留心等着听；偷听
definition_en: to give deliberate attention to sound, to heed what is said, to wait for a particular sound, or to overhear a conversation
core_image: 一个人停下手里的活，侧耳朝向声音来源
scene: 夜里屋子很静，母亲关掉电视，侧耳对着楼上婴儿床的方向。She turned down the radio and listened for the baby's cry.
sceneCN: 这里 listen 是「留心等着听」（第 3 个义项：等某个声音出现）；句意为她调低收音机，等着听婴儿的哭声。画面里可抓住的物件：关掉的电视、楼上的婴儿床、调低的音量。

senses.title: To give attention to sound
senses.titleCN: 听：把注意力放到声音上
senses.definition: to give deliberate attention to a sound or to someone speaking
senses.definitionCN: 有意识地把注意力放在某个声音或某人的说话上
senses.example: She listened to the rain on the roof until she fell asleep.
senses.exampleCN: 她听着屋顶上的雨声，直到睡着。
senses.why: Old English had hlysnan for attending to sound beside hyran for simply hearing; the two verbs split the work, and listen took the side of effort and attention rather than passive reception.
senses.whyCN: 古英语里 hlysnan 表示注意地听，hyran 表示听见；两个动词分工，listen 占了「费心去听」这一边，而不是被动接收。

senses.title: To heed advice or a warning
senses.titleCN: 听从：把听到的话当回事
senses.definition: to pay attention to advice, a warning, or a request and act on it
senses.definitionCN: 重视劝告、警告或请求并照着去做
senses.example: He never listens to his doctor about sleep.
senses.exampleCN: 他从不听医生关于睡眠的建议。
senses.why: Hearing turns into obedience when the listener acts on what was said; the same verb slides from the ear to behaviour, which is why listen to reason and listen to your parents sound natural.
senses.whyCN: 当听的人照着话去做，听见就变成了服从；同一个动词从耳朵滑到行为，所以 listen to reason（听劝）和听父母的话都很自然。

senses.title: To wait and watch for a particular sound
senses.titleCN: 留心等着听：等某个声音出现
senses.definition: to keep one's attention on the possibility of a particular sound, especially in order to respond
senses.definitionCN: 把注意力放在某个可能出现的声响上，以便及时反应
senses.example: The guard listened for footsteps on the stairs.
senses.exampleCN: 守卫留神听着楼梯上的脚步声。
senses.why: The preposition for turns listening into a search: nothing has been heard yet, and the ear is held open for a signal, as in listen for the doorbell.
senses.whyCN: 介词 for 把「听」变成「找」：此刻还没有声音，只是把耳朵开着等一个信号，如留神听门铃。

senses.title: To overhear others on purpose
senses.titleCN: 偷听：躲在暗处听别人说话
senses.definition: to hear a conversation that is not meant for you, often by staying hidden or by using a device
senses.definitionCN: 听到并非说给自己听的谈话，常靠躲藏或借助设备
senses.example: Someone was listening in on the meeting from the next room.
senses.exampleCN: 有人躲在隔壁房间偷听会议。
senses.why: The particle in adds the idea of entering a space that is not yours, so listen in on marks the listener as an outsider who was never invited.
senses.whyCN: 小品词 in 加进「进入不属于自己的空间」的意思，所以 listen in on 把听者标成未被邀请的外人。

intro.en: Listen goes back to a Germanic verb for hearing with attention; the h of its Old English form was later dropped, and the word is widely linked to the root behind loud.
intro.cn: listen 源自日耳曼语中表示「用心听」的动词；古英语形式里的 h 后来被丢掉，一般认为它与 loud 同源。

items.en: The reconstructed root *ḱlew- meant to hear, and it also underlies words for fame, since being heard of is being talked about.
items.cn: 重构词根 *ḱlew- 意为「听见」，也衍生出表示名声的词，因为被人听说就是被人谈论。

items.en: *hlusinōn, a verb of listening, grew beside *hlūdaz, the adjective that became loud; both point back to the act of hearing.
items.cn: *hlusinōn 是表示「听」的动词，与后来变成 loud 的形容词 *hlūdaz 并生；两者都指向「听见」这一行为。

items.en: Old English wrote the verb as hlysnan, with an h that speakers later stopped pronouncing.
items.cn: 古英语把动词写作 hlysnan，词首的 h 后来在口语中不再发音。

items.en: Middle English settled on listen, dropped the h in spelling, and kept the meaning of giving ear to something.
items.cn: 中古英语定型为 listen，拼写中去掉 h，保留「把耳朵给某物」的意思。

items.en: Modern English adds listener and listening, and the phrasal forms listen in and listen up, which push the word toward eavesdropping and toward a call for attention.
items.cn: 现代英语派生 listener 与 listening，并发展出 listen in、listen up 等短语，把词义推向偷听与提醒注意。

note.en: The look-alike group collects forms built with listen; the near-meaning group separates deliberate listening from mere hearing and from related acts of attention.
note.cn: 形近组收由 listen 构成的词形；近义组把刻意的「听」与单纯的「听见」以及相关的注意行为区分开。

normalIntro.en: The word is carried by an Old English verb, its lost h, a Germanic root shared with loud, and English endings that make a listener and a listening.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词由古英语动词、失落了的 h、与 loud 共有的日耳曼词根，以及构成 listener 与 listening 的英语词尾共同支撑。

normal.en: Old English wrote the verb with an h, so the silent letter in today's spelling is a leftover, not a rule about pronunciation.
normal.cn: 古英语写法带 h，所以今天拼写里的不发音字母是遗留物，并不是发音规则。

normal.en: Listener is listen plus -er, the person at the receiving end of the sound.
normal.cn: listener 是 listen 加 -er，指声音接收端的那个人。

normal.en: Hear is what happens to you; listen is what you decide to do, and English keeps both verbs.
normal.cn: hear 是发生在你身上的事，listen 是你决定去做的事，英语把两个动词都保留下来。

normal.en: Listen for waits for a signal; listen to receives what is already there; the preposition marks the difference.
normal.cn: listen for 是等一个信号，listen to 是接收已经在那里的声音，介词标出了这个差别。

normal.en: Listen in on adds in because the listener steps into a space where he was not invited.
normal.cn: listen in on 之所以加 in，是因为听者走进了没有邀请他的空间。

abstract.en: To listen is to lend someone your ears for a while, which is why the verb so easily turns into obedience.
abstract.cn: 倾听是把耳朵借给别人一段时间，所以这个动词很容易变成服从。

abstract.en: Attention has a direction: you can listen to, listen for, or listen in, and each preposition draws a different boundary.
abstract.cn: 注意力是有方向的：可以 listen to、listen for、listen in，每个介词都画出不同的边界。

abstract.en: A word for hearing can grow into a word for trust, because people who are heard are also more likely to be followed.
abstract.cn: 表示「听」的词能长成表示「信任」的词，因为被听见的人也更容易被跟随。

definition_zh: 活泼的；充满活力的；生动的；热闹的；鲜艳的；热烈的
definition_en: full of energy and enthusiasm, vivid and full of interest, busy with activity, bright in colour, or vigorous in argument
core_image: 一群孩子在院子里追着皮球跑，笑声把安静的午后掀了起来
scene: 午后的院子里，几个孩子追着皮球跑，笑声一阵接一阵。The lively children kept the whole street awake with their shouting.
sceneCN: 这里 lively 是「活泼的」（第 1 个义项：精力充沛、爱动）；句意为这些活泼的孩子用喊声让整条街都醒着。图中可辨识物件：院子、皮球、奔跑的孩子。

pos.zh: 活泼的；生动的；热闹的；鲜艳的；热烈的

senses.title: Full of energy and enthusiasm
senses.definition: full of energy, movement and enthusiasm, especially in the way a person or animal behaves
senses.definitionCN: 充满精力、动作与热情，尤指人或动物的举止
senses.example: The lively children kept the whole street awake with their shouting.
senses.exampleCN: 这些活泼的孩子用喊声让整条街都醒着。
senses.why: Old English liflic joins lif, life, to -lic, the suffix of likeness; the first sense is a creature visibly full of life, moving and making sound.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 liflic 把 lif（生命）与表示「像……一样」的后缀 -lic 连在一起；最早的义项就是看得见生命在动的活物，会跑会叫。

senses.title: Vivid and full of interest
senses.definition: vivid, interesting and full of imaginative detail, as in a lively description or a lively imagination
senses.definitionCN: 生动有趣、充满想象细节，如生动的描写或丰富的想象力
senses.example: She gave a lively account of the market on a rainy morning.
senses.exampleCN: 她把雨中清晨的集市讲得活灵活现。
senses.why: A description that keeps moving in the mind is felt to have life; the energy of a body is transferred to words, so a vivid account is called lively.
senses.whyCN: 一段在脑海里不断活动的描写会被觉得有生命；身体的能量转移到了文字上，于是生动的叙述就被称作 lively。

senses.title: Busy and full of activity
senses.definition: full of people, movement and excitement, as a place or an event
senses.definitionCN: 充满人群、动静与兴奋感，用来形容地方或活动
senses.example: The square becomes lively after the shops close.
senses.exampleCN: 商店打烊之后，广场就热闹起来。
senses.why: A crowd moves and makes noise like one large body; a place that will not stay quiet borrows the same word.
senses.whyCN: 人群又动又响，像一个巨大的身体；一个安静不下来的地方就借用了同一个词。

senses.title: Bright and strong in colour
senses.definition: of colour, bright and strong enough to catch the eye immediately
senses.definitionCN: 指颜色明亮强烈，一眼就能抓住视线
senses.example: The walls were painted a lively shade of orange.
senses.exampleCN: 墙壁被刷成一种鲜艳的橙色。
senses.why: Strong colour jumps at the eye the way a moving body does; the visual shock is read as a sign of life.
senses.whyCN: 浓烈的颜色像活动的身体一样跳进眼里；这种视觉冲击被读成生命力的标志。

senses.title: Vigorous and full of argument
senses.definition: of a discussion, debate or game, energetic and full of strong, differing views
senses.definitionCN: 指讨论、辩论或比赛充满劲头，带着强烈而不同的意见
senses.example: The proposal led to a lively debate in the council.
senses.exampleCN: 这项提议在议事会里引发了一场激烈的辩论。
senses.why: A debate that keeps returning and refuses to settle behaves like a restless creature; the energy of life is lent to argument.
senses.whyCN: 一场反复回到原点、不肯定论的辩论，举止就像一个停不下来的活物；生命的劲头被借给了争论。

intro.en: Lively began as a Germanic compound meaning life-like, and it gradually shifted from living creatures to vivid speech, bright colour and busy places.
intro.cn: lively 最初是一个意为「像生命一样的」日耳曼语复合词，后来逐渐从活物转到生动的言语、鲜亮的颜色和热闹的地方。

items.en: Old English liflic meant living or having life, built from lif, life, and the suffix -lic.
items.cn: 古英语 liflic 意为有生命的、活着的，由 lif（生命）与后缀 -lic 构成。

items.en: The noun is reconstructed as libam, the ancestor of life; the suffix -lic is related to German -lich and English -ly.
items.cn: 这个词的名词部分一般重构为 libam，是 life 的祖先；后缀 -lic 与德语 -lich、英语 -ly 同源。

items.en: Middle English lively kept the sense living and began to mean active, quick and cheerful.
items.cn: 中古英语的 lively 保留了「活着的」义项，并开始表示活跃、轻快、快活。

items.en: By the sixteenth century lively could describe vivid speech, bright colour and busy places, not only living creatures.
items.cn: 到十六世纪，lively 已能形容生动的言辞、鲜亮的颜色和热闹的地方，不再只用于活物。

items.en: Modern English uses lively mainly for energy and vividness; the older sense of living survives in a few fixed phrases such as a lively hope.
items.cn: 现代英语的 lively 主要用于表示活力与生动；较旧的「活着的」义项只留在少数固定说法里，如 a lively hope。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the Germanic word for life; the near-meaning group gathers words for energy, vividness and busy activity.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在日耳曼语「生命」一词上的词；近义组收表示精力、生动与忙碌活动的词。

normalIntro.en: The word joins the Germanic noun for life to a suffix of likeness, and its family keeps returning to living energy and vivid movement.

normal.en: Old English liflic is life plus -lic, the suffix that became -ly; lively literally means life-like.
normal.cn: 古英语 liflic 是 life 加 -lic，也就是后来变成 -ly 的那个后缀；lively 字面上就是「像生命一样的」。

normal.en: The same suffix -ly appears in friendly and lovely, turning nouns into adjectives about a quality.
normal.cn: 同一个后缀 -ly 也出现在 friendly 与 lovely 里，把名词变成表示某种性质的形容词。

normal.en: Life, live and alive are close relatives, so a lively room is a room that seems to be alive.
normal.cn: life、live 与 alive 是近亲，所以一间 lively 的屋子就像一间活着的屋子。

normal.en: The word first described a living, moving body, and only later described speech, colour and markets.
normal.cn: 这个词最早描述会动会叫的活物，后来才用来描述言语、颜色和市场。

normal.en: Liveliness adds -ness to lively, naming the quality that a lively person or place shows.
normal.cn: liveliness 在 lively 后加 -ness，用来指活泼的人或地方所表现出的那种性质。

abstract.en: A lively room is one that behaves like a body: it moves, makes sound and will not sit still.
abstract.cn: 一间 lively 的屋子举止像个身体：会动、会响、不肯安静。

abstract.en: We call a description lively when reading it feels like watching something happen.
abstract.cn: 我们把一段描写称作 lively，是因为读它时像在看事情发生。

abstract.en: Bright colour and heated debate share the word because both refuse to stay quiet.
abstract.cn: 鲜艳的颜色与激烈的辩论共用这个词，因为两者都不肯安静。

definition_zh: 当地的；本地的；局部的；本地人；住处附近的酒吧；每站都停的慢车
definition_en: relating to a particular area or neighbourhood, affecting only one part of the body, a person who lives nearby, the pub nearest one's home, or a train that stops at every station
core_image: 街角一家小店的木牌上写着本街的名字，推门进去的人多半互相认识
scene: 周末的集市上，摊主把自家菜园刚摘的蔬菜摆上木桌，牌子上写着村子的名字。We bought honey from a local farmer at the market.
sceneCN: 这里 local 是「当地的」（第 1 个义项：属于某一地方的）；句意为我们在集市上从一位当地农夫那里买了蜂蜜。图中可辨识物件：木桌、菜蔬、写着村名的木牌。

pos.zh: 本地人；住处附近的酒吧；慢车

derivatives.zh: 由 local 加 -ly 构成，义为「在当地；局部地」
由 local 加 -ity 构成，义为「地点；地区」
由 local 加 -ize 构成，义为「使限于局部；定位」

senses.title: Belonging to a particular area
senses.definition: belonging to or connected with a particular small area, town or neighbourhood
senses.definitionCN: 属于或与某一小片区域、城镇或街区有关的
senses.example: We bought honey from a local farmer at the market.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在集市上从一位当地农夫那里买了蜂蜜。
senses.why: Latin locus means place, and the adjective built on it simply marks whatever belongs to one place rather than to the whole country.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 locus 意为「地方」，由它构成的形容词只是标记某物属于某一处，而不是属于整个国家。

senses.title: A person who lives in the area
senses.definition: a person who lives in a particular area, especially as opposed to a visitor
senses.definitionCN: 住在某一地区的人，尤指相对于外来访客而言
senses.example: The locals were friendly and pointed us towards the old bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 当地人都很友善，还给我们指了去老桥的路。
senses.why: If an adjective can label anything of a place, it can stand alone as a name for the people of that place, so the adjective turned into a countable noun.
senses.whyCN: 既然这个形容词能标记属于某地的一切，它就能单独出来指那个地方的人，于是形容词变成了可数名词。

senses.title: The pub nearest one's home
senses.definition: in British informal speech, the pub close to where one lives and goes regularly
senses.definitionCN: 英式非正式说法，指住家附近、常去的那家酒吧
senses.example: We spent the evening at our local, talking to the barman.
senses.exampleCN: 我们晚上待在住处附近那家酒吧，和酒保聊天。
senses.why: British drinkers shorten the phrase the local pub to the local, so the adjective absorbs its noun and becomes a familiar place with a definite article.
senses.whyCN: 英国喝酒的人把 the local pub 缩成 the local，形容词吞掉了它修饰的名词，成了一个带定冠词的熟悉去处。

senses.title: Affecting only one part of the body
senses.definition: affecting only a small area of the body rather than the whole of it
senses.definitionCN: 只影响身体的一小块区域，而不是全身
senses.example: The dentist gave her a local anaesthetic before drilling.
senses.exampleCN: 牙医在钻牙之前给她用了局部麻醉。
senses.why: Medicine needed a word for treatment confined to one spot, and the adjective for belonging to a place was ready to mark a boundary inside the body.
senses.whyCN: 医学需要一个词来表示只限于某一处的治疗，而那个表示「属于某地」的形容词正好能在身体内部划出边界。

senses.title: A train that stops at every station
senses.definition: a train or bus that stops at every station along its route, in American usage
senses.definitionCN: 美式用法中指沿途每站都停的火车或公共汽车
senses.example: He took the local instead of the express and watched the small towns go by.
senses.exampleCN: 他坐了慢车而不是快车，一路上看着小镇慢慢退后。
senses.why: Railway timetables contrasted the express with the train serving each locality, and the name of the small place became the name of the slow service.
senses.whyCN: 铁路时刻表把快车与逐站服务各处的车对立起来，于是「小地方」的名字成了慢车的名字。

intro.en: Local goes back to the Latin word for place; the adjective travelled through French and then grew noun uses for people, pubs and trains.
intro.cn: local 可一直追到拉丁语中表示「地方」的词；这个形容词经法语进入英语，后来又长出指人、指酒吧和指慢车的名词用法。

items.en: Locus was the ordinary Latin noun for a place or a position, and its verb locare meant to put something in a place.
items.cn: locus 是拉丁语中表示地方或位置的普通名词，它的动词 locare 意为把某物放到某处。

items.en: Medieval Latin formed localis for whatever belongs to a particular place, and the adjective carried that narrow sense forward.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语造出 localis，指属于某一特定地方的东西，这个形容词把这层狭窄的意思继续传下去。

items.en: Old French used local as an adjective of place, and English borrowed it in the late fourteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语用 local 作为表示地方的形容词，英语在十四世纪晚期把它借了过来。

items.en: English applied local to parishes, customs and news, and in the nineteenth century began using it as a noun for the people and services of a place.
items.cn: 英语把 local 用于教区、习俗与新闻，并在十九世纪开始把它当名词，指一地的人和设施。

items.en: Modern English keeps local for the neighbourhood, medicine for a limited area of the body, British speech for the nearby pub, and American timetables for the stopping train.
items.cn: 现代英语用 local 指邻里，医学用它指身体的局部，英式口语用它指附近的酒吧，美式时刻表用它指逐站停靠的慢车。

normalIntro.en: The word is built on the Latin noun for place, and its family keeps returning to position, neighbourhood and the services of one small area.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词建立在拉丁语表示「地方」的名词上，它的同族词反复回到位置、邻里，以及某一小片区域的设施。

normal.en: Latin locus means place, so local is literally the adjective of a place, not of a whole country.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 locus 意为地方，所以 local 字面就是「属于某地的」形容词，而不是属于整个国家的。

normal.en: Locality adds -ity to local and names the area itself, while locate returns to the Latin verb for placing.
normal.cn: locality 在 local 后加 -ity，直接指那片区域；locate 则回到拉丁语中表示「放置」的动词。

normal.en: Local time is the time of one meridian, which is why a flight announcement always names it.
normal.cn: local time 是某一条经线上的时间，所以航班广播总要说明是当地时间。

normal.en: British speakers call their regular pub the local, shortening the local pub to one familiar word.
normal.cn: 英国人说 the local 指自己常去的酒吧，把 the local pub 缩成一个熟悉的词。

normal.en: A local train stops at each locality, so the adjective for small places became a noun for slow service.
normal.cn: local train 在每一个小地方都停，于是「小地方」的形容词变成了慢车的名词。

abstract.en: One adjective for place can name the people, the pub and the train, because all three are defined by being near.
abstract.cn: 同一个表示地方的形容词能指人、指酒吧、指火车，因为这三者都由「近」来定义。

abstract.en: Local and regional both answer where, but local draws a much smaller circle around the speaker.
abstract.cn: local 与 regional 都在回答「在哪里」，但 local 在说话者周围画出的圈小得多。

abstract.en: Medicine borrows the word to draw a border inside the body, showing how a place word can be used for any limited area.
abstract.cn: 医学借这个词在身体内部划一条边界，说明一个表示地方的词可用于任何有限的范围。

examples.en: We bought honey from a local farmer at the market.
examples.cn: 我们在集市上从一位当地农夫那里买了蜂蜜。

examples.en: The locals were friendly and pointed us towards the old bridge.
examples.cn: 当地人都很友善，还给我们指了去老桥的路。

examples.en: The dentist gave her a local anaesthetic before drilling.
examples.cn: 牙医在钻牙之前给她用了局部麻醉。

sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「属于某一处」；义项由此分成那地方的人、附近的酒吧、身体的局部，以及每个小站都停的慢车。

senses.title: A particular place or position
senses.definition: the place where someone or something is, or where an event happens
senses.definitionCN: 某人或某物所在、或某事发生的地方
senses.example: The hotel is in a quiet location near the park.
senses.exampleCN: 这家旅馆位于公园附近一处安静的地段。
senses.why: Latin locatio named the act of placing something, and English turned that act into the place that results from it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 locatio 指「放置」这个动作，英语由此转而指放置之后形成的那个地点。

senses.title: The act of finding where something is
senses.definition: the process of discovering or fixing the exact place of something
senses.definitionCN: 发现或确定某物确切位置的过程
senses.example: The location of the missing boat took the coast guard three days.
senses.exampleCN: 找到那条失踪小船的位置花了海岸警卫队三天。
senses.why: The noun can still name the action behind the place, so it covers the search as well as the spot finally found.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词仍能指地点背后的动作，所以既能指找到的那个点，也能指寻找这件事。

senses.title: A place used for filming outside a studio
senses.definition: a real place used for shooting a film or television scene instead of a built set
senses.definitionCN: 用来拍摄电影或电视场景的真实地点，而不是搭建的布景
senses.example: The crew spent two weeks at a mountain location.
senses.exampleCN: 摄制组在一个山区外景地待了两周。
senses.why: Film work needed a word for the real place standing in for a fictional one, and location was ready to carry that meaning.
senses.whyCN: 影视工作需要一个词来指代替代虚构场景的真实地点，location 正好承接了这个意思。

senses.title: A position in memory or on a disk
senses.definition: a place in a computer's memory or storage where a piece of data is kept
senses.definitionCN: 计算机内存或存储中保存某条数据的位置
senses.example: The program writes each record to a fixed location in memory.
senses.exampleCN: 程序把每条记录写到内存中一个固定的位置。
senses.why: Once a place can be pointed to precisely, machines borrow the word for the address where data sits.
senses.whyCN: 一旦一个地点能被精确指出，机器也用这个词来指数据所在的地址。

intro.en: Location is the Latin noun for a placing, built on the verb to place, and it reached English through French.
intro.cn: location 是拉丁语中表示「放置」的名词，建立在动词「放置」之上，经法语进入英语。

items.en: The Latin noun locus meant a place or spot and supplied the stem for the whole family.
items.cn: 拉丁语名词 locus 意为地方、地点，为整族词提供了词干。

items.en: The verb locare meant to place or set something somewhere, and it gave the action behind the noun.
items.cn: 动词 locare 意为把某物放置在某处，提供了名词背后的动作。

items.en: Locatio named a placing, and in legal Latin it could also mean a letting or a lease of property.
items.cn: locatio 指放置，在拉丁法律用语里也可指财产的出租。

items.en: Old French location carried the sense of a lease or a placing, and English borrowed the form.
items.cn: 古法语 location 带有出租或安置的意思，英语借用了这个词形。

items.en: Modern English made location the ordinary word for a place, then extended it to film sets and memory addresses.
items.cn: 现代英语让 location 成为指地点的常用词，随后扩展到影视外景与内存地址。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words on the Latin stem of placing; the near-meaning group collects nouns for a place in space.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁「放置」词干上的词；近义组收表示空间位置的各类名词。

normalIntro.en: Location is the noun of placing: it can name the act, the resulting spot, and the special places films and computers point to.
normalIntro.cn: location 是「放置」的名词形式：它能指动作，能指由此形成的地点，也能指影视与计算机特指的位置。

normal.en: Location comes from Latin locatio, a placing, built on the verb locare.
normal.cn: location 来自拉丁语 locatio，意为放置，建立在动词 locare 之上。

normal.en: The suffix -tion turns the act of placing into the thing or result, here the place itself.
normal.cn: 后缀 -tion 把「放置」这个动作变成事物或结果，在这里就是那个地点。

normal.en: On location is a film phrase: the crew shoots where the story is supposed to happen.
normal.cn: on location 是影视用语：剧组在故事该发生的地方实拍。

normal.en: Locate is the verb, location the noun, and both keep the same Latin stem.
normal.cn: locate 是动词，location 是名词，两者共用同一拉丁词干。

normal.en: A prime location is one that everyone wants, which shows the word carries value as well as position.
normal.cn: prime location 指人人都想要的地段，说明这个词除位置之外还带着价值判断。

abstract.en: A place becomes a word only when someone needs to point at it.
abstract.cn: 一个地方只有在有人需要指认它时才变成一个词。

abstract.en: Location turns empty space into a spot with a name and a purpose.
abstract.cn: location 把空白的空间变成一个有名字、有用途的点。

abstract.en: The word travels from leases to film sets to memory chips without losing its centre.
abstract.cn: 这个词从租约走到片场，再到内存芯片，始终没有丢掉中心。

examples.en: The meeting will be held at a location outside the city centre.

definition_zh: 锁；锁具；锁上；卡住；一绺头发；船闸
definition_en: to fasten something with a key or a catch, or the fastening device itself, a strand of hair, or a canal gate
core_image: 钥匙一转，锁舌滑进扣槽，门与门框从此扣成一体
scene: 夜里的院门半掩着，她伸手把铁锁扣好才上楼。She locked the gate and checked it twice before leaving.
sceneCN: 这里是「锁上、用锁锁住」（第 1 个义项：用钥匙或扣件把门关牢）；句意为她把院门锁好，走前还检查了两遍。可辨物件：院门、铁锁、楼道灯。

senses.title: To fasten something with a lock
senses.definition: to close and secure a door, box or vehicle with a key or a catch so that it cannot be opened easily
senses.definitionCN: 用钥匙或扣件把门、箱子或车辆关紧，使别人不容易打开
senses.example: She locked the door and put the key in her pocket.
senses.exampleCN: 她锁上门，把钥匙放进口袋。
senses.why: The Old English noun loc named the fastening itself, and the verb grew out of the act of turning that fastening shut.
senses.whyCN: 古英语名词 loc 本指扣件本身，动词义就是从「把这扣件扣上」这个动作长出来的。

senses.title: To become stuck and unable to move
senses.definition: to become fixed in one position, so that a part cannot turn or move freely
senses.definitionCN: 固定在某个位置，使某个部件无法转动或自由活动
senses.example: The wheels locked when he hit the brake hard.
senses.exampleCN: 他猛踩刹车时车轮抱死了。
senses.why: Once a lock is shut, nothing moves through it; applied to machines, the same image means a part that will not turn.
senses.whyCN: 锁一旦扣上，什么东西都过不去；用在机械上，同一个意象就指再也转不动的部件。

senses.title: The fastening device itself
senses.definition: a device with a key, a dial or a code that keeps a door or container shut
senses.definitionCN: 用钥匙、转盘或密码让门或容器保持关闭的装置
senses.example: The old trunk had a heavy brass lock.
senses.exampleCN: 这只旧箱子配着一把沉重的黄铜锁。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense, the thing you hold in your hand, and every other sense spreads out from it.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的义项，即你手里握着的那个物件，其余义项都从它扩散出去。

senses.title: A strand or small bunch of hair
senses.definition: a small quantity of hair that hangs or grows together as one piece
senses.definitionCN: 共同垂下或长在一起的一小束头发
senses.example: A lock of hair fell across her forehead.
senses.exampleCN: 一绺头发垂落在她额前。
senses.why: Hair that holds together in one clump looks like something fastened, so the word for a fastening was reused for a bunch of hair.
senses.whyCN: 头发聚成一束，看起来就像被扣住的东西，于是表示扣件的词又被用来指一束头发。

senses.title: A section of a canal with gates
senses.definition: a part of a canal closed off by gates, where the water level is raised or lowered for boats
senses.definitionCN: 运河上用闸门隔出的一段，通过升降水位让船只通过
senses.example: The barge waited for the lock to fill with water.
senses.exampleCN: 驳船等着船闸注满水。
senses.why: A canal lock works by shutting water in or out, which is exactly what a lock does to a door.
senses.whyCN: 船闸靠把水关进或放出而工作，这正是锁对门所做的那件事。

intro.en: Lock is a native English word whose deeper Germanic origin is reconstructed rather than recorded, and it has no reliable Latin relative.
intro.cn: lock 是英语本土词，更早的日耳曼语来源属于重构而非有记录的原形，也没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

items.en: The fastening is generally traced to a Germanic root luk-, whose exact shape is reconstructed rather than recorded.
items.cn: 这类扣件一般认为可追到日耳曼语词根 luk-，其确切形式属于重构，而不是有记录的原形。

items.en: Old English loc meant a fastening, a bolt or a barrier, and it also named a lock of hair.
items.cn: 古英语 loc 指扣件、门闩或障碍，同时也指一绺头发。

items.en: Middle English lock kept both the device and the hair sense, and the verb locken appeared for shutting something with it.
items.cn: 中古英语 lock 同时保留器具与头发两个义项，动词 locken 出现，表示用锁具关住。

items.en: Modern English added canal locks, and the verb widened to mean any part that jams and will not move.
items.cn: 现代英语增添了船闸义，动词也扩展到指任何卡住不动的部件。

items.en: Today the word covers keys and doors, traffic queues, canal gates, and a single strand of hair.
items.cn: 今天这个词覆盖钥匙与门、排队的车辆、船闸闸门以及一束头发。

normalIntro.en: Lock is an Old English word for a fastening, and its many senses all come from one picture: something held shut.
normalIntro.cn: lock 是古英语中表示扣件的词，它的众多义项都出自同一个画面：某样东西被扣住不放。

normal.en: Lock is an Old English word for a fastening, older than any Latin borrowing in this entry.
normal.cn: lock 是古英语中表示扣件的词，比这条词条里的任何拉丁借词都古老。

normal.en: Unlock is simply un- plus lock, the prefix undoing the fastening.
normal.cn: unlock 就是 un- 加 lock，前缀把扣紧的状态解掉。

normal.en: A lock of hair is not a different word: hair that holds together looks fastened.
normal.cn: a lock of hair 并不是另一个词：头发聚成一束，看起来像被扣住了。

normal.en: Lock up, lock in and lock out all keep the same core of shutting something in or out.
normal.cn: lock up、lock in 与 lock out 都保留着「把东西关进或关外」这同一个核心。

normal.en: A canal lock locks water in or out, which is why the same word serves boats and doors.
normal.cn: 船闸把水关进或放出，所以同一个词能同时用于船和门。

abstract.en: A lock is a promise made in metal: only the right person passes.
abstract.cn: 锁是用金属做出的承诺：只有对的人才能通过。

abstract.en: When a wheel locks, the machine briefly behaves like a shut door.
abstract.cn: 车轮抱死时，机器短暂地像一扇关上的门。

abstract.en: The word joins a keyhole, a hair strand and a canal gate because all three are things that hold together or shut.
abstract.cn: 这个词把钥匙孔、一束头发和闸门连在一起，因为三者都是「扣住」或「关住」的东西。

examples.en: Remember to lock the back door before you leave.
examples.cn: 走之前记得把后门锁上。

examples.en: A thick lock of hair fell over her eyes.
examples.cn: 厚厚一绺头发垂到她眼睛上。

examples.en: The ship waited for the lock gates to open.
examples.cn: 船等着闸门打开。

sensesIntro.en: The core is something held shut; the senses then spread from the device to its action, to a jammed part, to a clump of hair and to a canal gate.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「被扣住不放」；义项由器具扩散到动作、卡死的部件、一束头发，以及运河闸门。

core.cn: 核心意象：钥匙一转，锁舌滑进扣槽，门与门框扣成一体。

definition_zh: 孤独的；寂寞的；偏僻的；荒凉的；孤零零的
definition_en: unhappy because one lacks company; (of a place) far from others and rarely visited; standing apart with nothing similar nearby
core_image: 深夜的公交站牌下，只有一个人影和一条长长的影子
scene: 雪停了，屋檐下的灯还亮着，屋里只有一个人。She felt lonely in the new flat, even though the street outside was full of noise.
sceneCN: 这里是「因缺少陪伴而难受」（第 1 个义项：独自一人时感到寂寞）；句意为虽然外面的街道很吵，她在新公寓里仍然觉得寂寞。

pos.zh: 孤独的；寂寞的；偏僻的；荒凉的

senses.title: Sad because one has no company
senses.definition: unhappy because one lacks company or close contact with other people
senses.definitionCN: 因为缺少陪伴或与他人的亲近接触而难受
senses.example: He grew lonely after his closest friends moved away.
senses.exampleCN: 最亲近的朋友搬走以后，他变得孤独起来。
senses.why: Lone means being just one, and -ly turns that state into a feeling; the pain comes from having nobody to answer you.
senses.whyCN: lone 意为「只有一个人」，-ly 把这种状态变成一种感受；难受的根源是身边没有人回应自己。

senses.title: Remote and rarely visited
senses.definition: of a place: far from other places, with few people passing through
senses.definitionCN: 指地方远离别处，很少有人经过
senses.example: The farm stood on a lonely stretch of the coast road.
senses.exampleCN: 那座农场孤零零地立在海岸公路的一段上。
senses.why: A place that is one by itself, far from any neighbour, borrows the human word for isolation and turns it into a description of distance.
senses.whyCN: 一个地方独自存在、离任何邻里都远，于是借用了写人的「孤立」一词，把它变成对距离的描述。

senses.title: Standing apart with nothing similar nearby
senses.titleCN: 孤零零的；旁边没有同样的东西
senses.definition: of a thing: standing alone, separated from others of its kind
senses.definitionCN: 指物体单独立着，和同类分开
senses.example: A lonely tree stood at the top of the hill.
senses.exampleCN: 山顶上立着一棵孤零零的树。
senses.why: From people to places and then to objects, the same shape repeats: one thing, no companion, a visible gap around it.
senses.whyCN: 从人扩展到地方，再扩展到物体，重复的是同一个形状：只有一样东西，没有同伴，四周留着一圈看得见的空。

intro.en: Lonely is built from lone, a shortened form of alone, which began as the Old English phrase for all one; the word for one lies underneath all of it.
intro.cn: lonely 由 lone 加后缀构成，而 lone 是 alone 的截短形式；alone 最初是古英语中「全部为一」的说法，底下站着的是表示「一」的词。

items.en: The English word one and Latin unus both descend from a shared Indo-European form for a single unit.
items.cn: 英语的 one 与拉丁语 unus 都来自印欧语系中表示「一个单位」的同一个形式。

items.en: An meant one, and al, meaning all, was joined to it, so al an said all one, that is, entirely by oneself.
items.cn: ān 意为「一」，表示「全部」的 al 加在前面，al an 就是「全部为一」，也就是完完全全只有自己。

items.en: The phrase was written as one word, alone, and speakers later clipped off the first syllable to make lone.
items.cn: 这个短语后来写成一个词 alone，再往后说话的人省掉了开头音节，得到了 lone。

items.en: Adding -ly to lone made lonely, which describes not the fact of being alone but the state of feeling it.
items.cn: 在 lone 后加 -ly 得到 lonely，它描述的不是独处的事实，而是独处带来的状态。

items.en: Modern English uses lonely for people, for remote places and for single objects standing apart from their kind.
items.cn: 现代英语用 lonely 写人、写偏僻的地方，也写单独立着、和同类分开的物体。

entries.definition: Done alone, or living alone by choice.

entries.definition: Far away from towns and other people.

normalIntro.en: Lonely rests on the old phrase for all one, so the word measures how far a person is from any other voice.
normalIntro.cn: lonely 立在古英语「全部为一」这个说法上，所以这个词量的是一个人离另一个声音有多远。

normal.en: Lonely comes from lone, and lone is alone with its first syllable clipped; alone literally said all one.
normal.cn: lonely 来自 lone，而 lone 是去掉开头音节的 alone；alone 字面就是「全部为一」。

normal.en: Alone states a fact and lonely states a feeling, which is why a person can be alone for a week without feeling lonely.
normal.cn: alone 说的是事实，lonely 说的是感受，所以一个人可以独处一周却不觉得寂寞。

normal.en: Add -ly to lone and you get lonely, the same suffix that builds friendly and lovely from nouns.
normal.cn: 在 lone 后加 -ly 就是 lonely，friendly 和 lovely 也是用同一个后缀从名词变来的。

normal.en: Loneliness adds -ness to lonely, turning a passing mood into a lasting condition.
normal.cn: loneliness 在 lonely 后加 -ness，把一时的情绪变成一种持续的状态。

normal.en: Lonesome is the American cousin; -some carries the sense of full of, so it is full of being alone.
normal.cn: lonesome 是美式英语的近亲；-some 带有「充满」的意味，所以它指「满是独处的感觉」。

abstract.en: All one is a picture before it is a phrase: a person pulling the whole world in until only himself is left.
abstract.cn: 「全部为一」先是一个画面，然后才是一个说法：一个人把整个世界收拢，直到只剩下自己。

abstract.en: A road and a tree can be lonely too, which shows English is willing to lend a human situation to the landscape.
abstract.cn: 一条路、一棵树也能用 lonely，说明英语愿意把人的处境借给风景。

abstract.en: When the lights, the heating and the street noise are all present and the person is still lonely, the word is counting echoes rather than neighbours.
abstract.cn: 灯、暖气和街上的喧闹都在，人却仍然 lonely，说明这个词数的是回应，而不是身边的人。

examples.en: She felt lonely on her first night in the city.
examples.cn: 她在这个城市的第一夜感到孤独。

examples.en: They walked along a lonely road for hours.
examples.cn: 他们在一条荒凉的路上走了几个小时。

examples.en: A lonely tree stood in the middle of the field.
examples.cn: 田野中央立着一棵孤零零的树。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「冷离」——冷冷地离开人群，身边空了，心里也就 lonely。

definition_zh: 看；瞧；看起来；显得；目光；一瞥；外观；样子；朝向
definition_en: to direct your eyes towards something; to seem or appear in a certain way; an act of looking, or the appearance of someone or something
core_image: 玻璃柜前，一双眼睛把画上的每一笔都慢慢扫过
scene: 展厅里人不多，一个女孩在画前站了很久。She looked at the painting for a long time before she spoke.
sceneCN: 这里是「把视线投向某物」（第 1 个义项：用眼睛去看）；句意为她在画前看了很久才开口。

derivatives.zh: 由 look 与 out 复合而成，义为「瞭望处；瞭望员」
由 on、look 与 -er 复合而成，义为「旁观者」

由 out 与 look 复合而成，义为「观点；前景」

senses.title: To direct the eyes at something
senses.definition: to turn your eyes towards something in order to see it
senses.definitionCN: 把眼睛转向某物，以便看见它
senses.example: Look at the map before you choose a route.
senses.exampleCN: 选路线之前先看看地图。
senses.why: Old English locian named the act of using the eyes, so the physical movement of attention is the base from which the other senses grow.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 lōcian 指的就是用眼睛去看，所以这个把注意力送出去的动作，是其余义项生长的根。

senses.title: To seem or appear a certain way
senses.definition: to seem or appear, judged from what the eye can see
senses.definitionCN: 根据眼睛能看到的情况作出判断；显得
senses.example: The soup looks hot enough to burn your tongue.
senses.exampleCN: 这汤看上去烫得能烫到舌头。
senses.why: What a thing looks like is the evidence the eye gathers, and English lets that evidence become a judgement, so a visible clue turns into a claim about the thing.
senses.whyCN: 一样东西看起来如何，是眼睛收集到的证据；英语让这份证据直接变成判断，于是看得见的线索变成了对事物的说法。

senses.title: The appearance of someone or something
senses.definition: the appearance of a person or thing, especially the impression it makes
senses.definitionCN: 人或物呈现出来的样子，尤指它给人的印象
senses.example: She gave the old bike a new look with a coat of paint.
senses.exampleCN: 她刷了一层漆，让那辆旧自行车有了新样子。
senses.why: The noun takes the verb's picture and fixes it: a look is what a thing presents to anyone who glances at it.
senses.whyCN: 名词把动词的画面固定下来：一个 look 就是一样东西呈现在任何瞥见它的人眼里的样子。

senses.title: A single act of looking
senses.definition: one short act of directing the eyes at something
senses.definitionCN: 把目光投向某物的一次短暂动作
senses.example: A quick look at the clock told him he was late.
senses.exampleCN: 他瞟了一眼钟，就知道自己迟到了。
senses.why: Counting the action gives a small unit, one turn of the eyes, which is why a look can be quick, long or stolen.
senses.whyCN: 把动作数出来就得到一个小单位，也就是眼睛转动的一回，所以 a look 可以是快的、久的，也可以是偷偷投过去的。

senses.title: To face a particular direction
senses.definition: of a building or room: to have its front or opening towards a place
senses.definitionCN: 指建筑或房间的正面或开口朝向某个方向
senses.example: The kitchen looks out over the garden.
senses.exampleCN: 厨房的窗子朝向花园。
senses.why: A building has a front, and the front is where it faces; English describes that facing as looking, as if the house had eyes.
senses.whyCN: 建筑有正面，正面就是它朝向的一边；英语把这种朝向说成 looking，仿佛房子也长了眼睛。

intro.en: Look goes back to an Old English verb for using the eyes, and its deeper origin is uncertain; the sense of seeming grew from the visible evidence a thing offers.
intro.cn: look 可以追到古英语中表示「用眼睛看」的动词，更早的来源不确定；「显得」这一义则从事物给出的可见证据上长出来。

items.en: Related forms appear in other West Germanic languages, but no earlier common source is established beyond doubt.
items.cn: 其他西日耳曼语中能看到相关的形式，但更早的共同来源并没有定论。

items.en: Locian meant to see or to look, and it described the act of turning the eyes towards something.
items.cn: lōcian 意为看、望，描述的是把眼睛转向某物的动作。

items.en: The verb survived as loken, and its spelling slowly moved towards the modern form with oo.
items.cn: 这个动词在中古英语中写作 lōken，拼写慢慢向带 oo 的现代形式靠拢。

items.en: Writers began using look with an adjective after it, so that a thing could look tired, fresh or dangerous.
items.cn: 早期现代英语的作者开始让 look 后面接形容词，于是一样东西可以看起来疲惫、新鲜或危险。

items.en: The word now covers seeing, seeming, appearance and direction, and it builds a large family of compounds.
items.cn: 现代英语中，这个词覆盖看、显得、外观和朝向，并构成一大族复合词。

note.en: The look-alike group is formed with out, on and alike; the near-meaning group gathers the main verbs of seeing and seeming.
note.cn: 形近组由 out、on、alike 等成分与 look 组合而成；近义组收表示看与显得的主要动词。

normalIntro.en: Look is a plain verb of the eyes that grew a second life as a verb of judgement, so seeing and seeming share one form.
normalIntro.cn: look 本是眼睛的动词，后来又长出判断的用法，于是「看见」和「显得」共用同一个形式。

normal.en: Old English locian meant to use the eyes, and the modern verb continues that physical act without interruption.
normal.cn: 古英语 lōcian 意为用眼睛看，现代动词直接继承了这一身体动作。

normal.en: Look after is literally to look behind someone, which is what caring for a person feels like: your eyes keep following them.
normal.cn: look after 字面是「在某人后面看」，照看一个人正是这种感觉：目光一直跟着他。

normal.en: Look forward to points the eyes ahead, so the phrase means waiting for something that has not happened yet.
normal.cn: look forward to 把眼睛朝前放，所以这个短语指等待还没发生的事。

normal.en: A lookout is look plus out: the person or place that watches outward for what is coming.
normal.cn: lookout 是 look 加 out：向外看、留意有什么过来的人或地方。

normal.en: Lookalike joins look and alike, two things that look the same without being the same.
normal.cn: lookalike 把 look 和 alike 拼在一起：看着一样，其实并不是同一个。

abstract.en: Looking is attention sent outward, which is why the verb so often needs at, for or into to say where the eyes land.
abstract.cn: 看是把注意力送出去，所以这个动词常要带 at、for 或 into，说明目光落在哪里。

abstract.en: One word for seeing and for seeming tells us how much English trusts the eye as a judge.
abstract.cn: 「看」和「显得」共用一个词，说明英语很相信眼睛作出的判断。

abstract.en: The look of a thing is the face it turns towards the world, so style, mood and expression can all fit inside the word.
abstract.cn: 一样东西的 look 是它朝向世界的那一面，所以风格、气氛和神情都能装进这个词。

examples.en: Look at the sky before you decide to go.
examples.cn: 出门之前先看看天。

examples.en: The room looks much bigger without the extra chairs.
examples.cn: 少了那几把多余的椅子，房间看起来大得多。

examples.en: He took one look at the letter and left the room.
examples.cn: 他看了一眼那封信，就离开了房间。

definition_zh: 大声地；响亮地；强烈地；花哨地
definition_en: in a way that makes a strong sound; also in an insistent or showy manner
core_image: 一个人站上台阶，张开嘴高声呼喊，声音一圈圈扩散到街角
scene: 排练室的门半开着，歌声和鼓点一阵高过一阵，楼上的住户都听见了。The choir sang loudly enough to carry through the whole building.
sceneCN: 这里 loudly 是「大声地、响亮地」（第 1 个义项）；句意为合唱团唱得足够响，声音传遍了整栋楼。画面里可认出半开的门、谱架和排练室。

pos.zh: 大声地；响亮地；强烈地；花哨地

derivatives.zh: 由 loudly 去掉副词后缀 -ly 得到的形容词，义为「响亮的；大声的」
由 loud 加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「响亮；音量」
由 loud 与 mouth 复合而成，义为「爱吹嘘、话多的人」

senses.title: At a high volume of sound
senses.definition: in a way that produces a strong, easily heard sound
senses.definitionCN: 以发出强烈、容易听见的声音的方式
senses.example: She called loudly for help from the balcony.
senses.exampleCN: 她在阳台上大声呼救。
senses.why: Loud comes from an old word for a strong sound, and -ly turns that quality into the way an action is done.
senses.whyCN: loud 来自表示强烈声响的古词，后缀 -ly 把这种性质变成了做动作的方式。

senses.title: With insistence, so as to be heard or noticed
senses.definition: in a forceful and public way, so that an opinion or complaint cannot be ignored
senses.definitionCN: 以有力而公开的方式，使某种意见或抱怨无法被忽视
senses.example: The residents protested loudly against the new road.
senses.exampleCN: 居民们大声抗议这条新路。
senses.why: If a sound is loud, it reaches many ears; the word therefore moves from volume to public pressure.
senses.whyCN: 声音如果响亮，就能传到很多耳朵里；因此这个词从音量转到公开施压。

senses.title: In a showy or garish manner
senses.definition: in a style that is too bright, bold or decorated to be quiet or tasteful
senses.definitionCN: 以过于鲜亮、大胆或繁复装饰、毫不含蓄的风格
senses.example: The room was loudly decorated with gold curtains and red walls.
senses.exampleCN: 这个房间用金色窗帘和红色墙面装饰得十分扎眼。
senses.why: A loud colour or pattern, like a loud sound, refuses to stay in the background, so the word extends from hearing to sight.
senses.whyCN: 花哨的颜色或图案就像响亮的声音一样不肯退到背景里，于是这个词从听觉延伸到视觉。

intro.en: Loudly is simply loud plus the adverb suffix -ly; loud itself goes back to an Old English word for a strong sound.
intro.cn: loudly 就是 loud 加上副词后缀 -ly；loud 本身可追溯到古英语中表示强烈声响的词。

items.en: The adjective hlūd meant loud or noisy, and it described both voices and the roar of a crowd.
items.cn: 形容词 hlūd 意为响亮的、喧闹的，既形容人声，也形容人群的轰鸣。

items.en: Its reconstructed ancestor is hlūdaz, a form rebuilt from comparison with related Germanic languages.
items.cn: 其重构祖形为 hlūdaz，这个形式是通过与相关日耳曼语言比较重建出来的。

items.en: Generally the word is traced to a root meaning to hear, which also stands behind Latin words for being renowned.
items.cn: 一般认为这个词可追溯到表示「听见」的词根，拉丁语中表示「有名」的词也出自此处。

items.en: Middle English kept loud, and speakers added -ly to make an adverb of manner.
items.cn: 中古英语保留 loud，说话者加 -ly 构成方式副词。

items.en: Modern English loudly covers high volume, insistent public speech and showy appearance.
items.cn: 现代英语的 loudly 涵盖高音量、公开坚持的表达以及花哨的外观。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words that share the loud root or are easily confused with loudly; the near-meaning group gathers other adverbs of sound and manner.
note.cn: 形近组收共用 loud 词根或容易与 loudly 混淆的词；近义组收其他表示声音与方式的副词。

normalIntro.en: The word is a transparent build: loud plus -ly. Its hooks therefore come from the root for sound, the suffix, and the way loud spreads from hearing to behaviour.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词的构造很透明：loud 加 -ly。记忆钩子因此来自表示声音的词根、后缀，以及 loud 从听觉扩展到行为的方式。

normal.en: Loudly is loud plus -ly, so the meaning is simply in a loud way.
normal.cn: loudly 是 loud 加 -ly，意思就是「以响亮的方式」。

normal.en: The older form hlūd already meant noisy, so the word has been about sound for a long time.
normal.cn: 更早的形式 hlūd 已经表示喧闹，所以这个词长期都与声音有关。

normal.en: Aloud uses the same root but means out loud rather than in a loud way.
normal.cn: aloud 用同一词根，但意思是「出声地」，而不是「大声地」。

normal.en: The comparative is more loudly, not loudlier, because the word already ends in -ly.
normal.cn: 比较级是 more loudly，而不是 loudlier，因为这个词本身已以 -ly 结尾。

normal.en: Loudly can follow protest and complain, where the volume is social pressure rather than decibels.
normal.cn: loudly 可以跟 protest、complain 搭配，此时「响」是社交压力而不是分贝。

abstract.en: A sound that is loud pushes into other people's space, and the adverb carries that same push into protest.
abstract.cn: 响亮的声音会挤进别人的空间，这个副词把同样的推力带进了抗议。

abstract.en: The move from a loud voice to a loud shirt shows that English treats both as things that refuse to be ignored.
abstract.cn: 从响亮的嗓音到花哨的衬衫，说明英语把两者都看成不肯被忽视的东西。

abstract.en: Adding -ly to a quality is like turning a colour into a way of painting: loud becomes the manner of the action.
abstract.cn: 给一种性质加 -ly，就像把颜色变成画法：loud 变成了动作的方式。

definition_zh: 低的；矮的；低落的；低声的；低点；低水平
definition_en: not high or tall; below the usual level, amount or value; also sad, quiet or deep in sound, and a lowest point
core_image: 一只手掌压向地面，把一根横杆缓缓降到几乎贴着泥土的位置
scene: 傍晚的球场边，一个孩子把球贴着草地滚出去，球一路几乎不离开泥土。The ball stayed low and skimmed over the wet grass.
sceneCN: 这里 low 是「低的、贴近地面的」（第 1 个义项：高度低）；句意为球一直贴着地面，从湿草上滑过去。画面里可认出球场边、草地与滚动的球。

pos.zh: 低的；矮的；低落的；低声的

derivatives.zh: low 的比较级形式兼作动词，义为「降低；放下」
由 low 加形容词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「卑微的；地位低的」
由前缀 be- 与 low 构成，义为「在……下面；低于」
由 low 加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「低；低落」

senses.title: Not high in height or position
senses.definition: having a small distance from the top to the ground, or standing near the ground
senses.definitionCN: 从顶部到地面的距离小，或位置接近地面的
senses.example: The shelf is low enough for a child to reach.
senses.exampleCN: 这个架子很低，孩子够得着。
senses.why: The oldest use describes a body or object near the ground, so lowness begins as a physical distance rather than a value.
senses.whyCN: 最早的用法描述人或物贴近地面的位置，所以「低」首先是一种空间距离，而不是价值判断。

senses.title: Below the usual level or amount
senses.definition: less than the normal, expected or average amount, level or value
senses.definitionCN: 低于正常、预期或平均的数量、水平或数值
senses.example: The river is unusually low this summer.
senses.exampleCN: 今年夏天这条河的水位异常低。
senses.why: Once the word can measure height, it can measure any scale, so a low river or a low price simply sits far down its own scale.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个词能度量高度，就能度量任何尺度，于是低水位、低价格只是在自己的尺度上位置很靠下。

senses.title: Sad, weak or without energy
senses.definition: feeling unhappy, tired or without hope and energy
senses.definitionCN: 感到不快、疲惫，或缺少希望与精力
senses.example: He felt low for weeks after moving to the new city.
senses.exampleCN: 搬到新城市后，他情绪低落了几个星期。
senses.why: A low position is close to the ground, and English links that downward picture with a lowered spirit, so the word moves from space to mood.
senses.whyCN: 低的位置贴近地面，英语把这幅向下的画面与低落的精神联系起来，于是词义从空间转到情绪。

senses.title: Soft in volume or deep in pitch
senses.definition: produced quietly, or having a deep pitch rather than a high one
senses.definitionCN: 以较小的音量发出，或音调低沉而不高尖的
senses.example: She answered in a low voice so the others would not hear.
senses.exampleCN: 她低声回答，免得别人听见。
senses.why: A deep note sits at the bottom of the scale and a quiet voice carries less force, so both are heard as a kind of downward position.
senses.whyCN: 低沉的音处在音阶底部，轻声说话的力量也更小，两者听起来都像一种向下的位置。

senses.title: A low point, level or area
senses.definition: a point or level that is the lowest reached, or an area of low pressure in weather
senses.definitionCN: 所达到的最低点或最低水平，也指天气图上气压较低的区域
senses.example: Sales reached a new low in the winter.
senses.exampleCN: 冬季销售额跌到了新的低点。
senses.why: Because the adjective can measure any scale, English turns it into a noun for the bottom value itself, and weather writers use it for low pressure.
senses.whyCN: 既然这个形容词能度量各种尺度，英语就把它变成名词，指最低的那个数值本身，气象作者又用它指低气压。

intro.en: Low is an Old English adjective for being near the ground; it later spread from height to amounts, mood and sound.
intro.cn: low 是古英语中表示贴近地面的形容词，后来从高度扩展到数量、情绪与声音。

items.en: The adjective lāh meant low or humble, and it could describe both the ground and a person's rank.
items.cn: 形容词 lāh 意为低的、卑微的，既能形容地面，也能形容人的地位。

items.en: The reconstructed form is lauha-, rebuilt from related Germanic words such as Dutch laag.
items.cn: 其重构形式为 lauha-，是通过荷兰语 laag 等相关日耳曼词重建出来的。

items.en: Middle English lowe kept the physical sense and began to describe prices, voices and spirits.
items.cn: 中古英语的 lowe 保留物理义，并开始形容价格、嗓音与情绪。

items.en: Writers extended the word to any scale that could be measured, from income to temperature.
items.cn: 作家把这个词扩展到任何可度量的尺度，从收入到温度。

items.en: Modern English uses low for height, level, mood and voice, and as a noun for the lowest point.
items.cn: 现代英语用 low 指高度、水平、情绪与嗓音，也用作名词指最低点。

note.cn: 形近组收 low 词族与一个拼写相近的词；近义组收表示高度小、深度小与地位低的词。

entries.definition: The comparative of low, also a verb meaning to bring down.
entries.definitionCN: low 的比较级，也可作动词表示降低。

entries.definition: Humble in rank or position; built from low with -ly.
entries.definitionCN: 地位或身份卑微的；由 low 加 -ly 构成。

entries.definition: Under or lower than something, built with be- and low.
entries.definitionCN: 在……下面或低于某物，由 be- 与 low 构成。

entries.definition: Not fast; only the spelling and rhyme are close, and the origin is different.
entries.definitionCN: 缓慢的；只是拼写与读音和 low 相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: Having little height when said of a person or thing.
entries.definitionCN: 形容人或物时表示个子矮、高度小。

entries.definition: Not deep, with little distance from top to bottom.
entries.definitionCN: 不深的，从顶到底距离很小。

entries.definition: Low in rank or importance, without pride.
entries.definitionCN: 地位或重要性低，不骄傲。

entries.definition: Making little or no sound.
entries.definitionCN: 发出很少声音或没有声音的。

entries.definition: Going far down from the top or surface.
entries.definitionCN: 从顶部或表面向下延伸很深的。

normalIntro.en: The word has been about being near the ground since Old English, and its family keeps returning to downward position, lower value and lowered feeling.
normalIntro.cn: 自古英语起这个词就表示贴近地面，同族词反复回到向下的位置、更低的值与低落的情绪。

normal.en: Old English lāh already meant low, so the word has kept its shape and sense for a very long time.
normal.cn: 古英语 lāh 已经表示低，所以这个词的形态与含义都保持了很长时间。

normal.en: The comparative is lower and the superlative is lowest, both made with the regular endings.
normal.cn: 比较级是 lower，最高级是 lowest，都用规则词尾构成。

normal.en: Below is be- plus low, literally at a lower place than something.
normal.cn: below 是 be- 加 low，字面就是「处于比某物更低的位置」。

normal.en: Low season names the quiet months of a trade, when prices and crowds are at their lowest.
normal.cn: low season 指行业的淡季，此时价格与客流都处在最低。

normal.en: Low point is a fixed phrase for the worst or weakest moment of a period.
normal.cn: low point 是固定说法，指一段时期里最糟或最弱的时刻。

abstract.en: A word that starts as a measurement of height ends up measuring mood, price and sound, because English reads downward as less.
abstract.cn: 一个从高度测量开始的词，最后用来测量情绪、价格与声音，因为英语把「向下」读作「更少」。

abstract.en: The same low note and low mood share a shape: both are felt as sinking rather than rising.
abstract.cn: 低沉的音与低落的情绪共享一种形状：两者都被感觉为下沉而不是上升。

abstract.en: A low point is only meaningful against a scale, which is why the word always implies something higher above it.
abstract.cn: 低点只有相对某个尺度才有意义，所以这个词总暗示着上方还有更高的东西。

examples.en: The shelf is low enough for a child to reach.
examples.cn: 这个架子很低，孩子够得着。

examples.en: The river is unusually low this summer.
examples.cn: 今年夏天这条河的水位异常低。

examples.en: She answered in a low voice so the others would not hear.
examples.cn: 她低声回答，免得别人听见。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「漏」——水往低处漏，位置越来越低，记住 low 是低。

root: 古英语 lāh（低的、卑微的），一般认为来自原始日耳曼语 lauha-，与荷兰语 laag 同源；没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is a position near the ground; the senses then measure level, mood, sound and finally the lowest point itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是贴近地面的位置；义项随后度量水平、情绪、声音，最后指最低点本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand pressing a bar down until it almost touches the soil.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手掌把一根横杆压到几乎贴着泥土的位置。

branches.en: a child rolling a ball along the grass
branches.cn: 孩子让球贴着草地滚动

branches.en: a river running far below its banks
branches.cn: 河水远低于河岸

branches.en: a newcomer alone in a rented room
branches.cn: 新来的人独坐在租来的房间里

branches.en: a whisper meant for one pair of ears
branches.cn: 只说给一双耳朵听的耳语

branches.en: a chart line falling to its worst value
branches.cn: 图表曲线跌到最差的数值

intro.en: Low is a short Germanic adjective that English has turned into comparison, a verb, a compound and a noun.
intro.cn: low 是一个简短的日耳曼语形容词，英语把它发展出比较级、动词、复合词与名词用法。

latinIntro.en: Low belongs to the Germanic family, so it has no reliable Latin cognate.
latinIntro.cn: low 属于日耳曼语族，因此没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

items.example: Old English lāh described both the ground and a person's rank.
items.exampleCN: 古英语 lāh 既形容地面，也形容人的地位。

items.meaning: near the ground or below a level
items.example: The wall was low enough to look over.
items.exampleCN: 这堵墙低得可以越过它看过去。

items.meaning: more low; also to bring down
items.example: The sun sank lower behind the hills.
The lake reaches its lowest level in autumn.
items.exampleCN: 湖泊在秋天达到最低水位。

items.example: He came from a lowly family but rose quickly.
items.exampleCN: 他出身卑微，却升得很快。

items.example: The valley lay below the clouds.

items.meaningCN: 形容词后缀：具有……性质的
items.example: Lowly adds -ly to low.

items.meaning: the quiet period of a trade
items.example: Hotels cut prices in the low season.

definition_zh: 运气；好运；侥幸；时运
definition_en: the force that seems to decide events by chance; also good fortune and success that comes without skill
core_image: 一枚硬币在空中翻转，落下时正好卡在指尖上方，摇摇欲坠却没有倒
scene: 码头边，渔夫把最后一网兜拉上来，网里空空的，可转身时却在木板上看见一枚别人掉下的硬币。Luck came to him at the very moment he had stopped expecting anything.
sceneCN: 这里 luck 是「好运、幸运」（第 2 个义项：带来好结果的好运）；句意为运气在他不再期待的时候降临。画面里可认出码头、空网兜与木板上的硬币。

derivatives.zh: 由 luck 加形容词后缀 -y 构成，义为「幸运的」
由 lucky 变 y 为 i 再加 -ly 构成，义为「幸运地；幸好」
由 luck 加表示「没有」的后缀 -less 构成，义为「运气不好的」

senses.title: Chance seen as a force that shapes events
senses.definition: the force that seems to decide events by chance, whether the outcome is good or bad
senses.definitionCN: 似乎在冥冥中决定事情成败的偶然力量，无论结果是好是坏
senses.example: No one can explain why the storm missed the village; they put it down to luck.
senses.exampleCN: 谁也说不清风暴为什么绕过了村子，他们把它归因于运气。
senses.why: When people cannot explain why a plan succeeds or fails, they name the unknown cause luck, so the word first stands in for chance itself.
senses.whyCN: 当人们说不清一个计划为何成功或失败时，就把这个未知的原因叫作 luck，所以这个词最初是「偶然本身」的代称。

senses.title: Good fortune that brings favourable results
senses.definition: good fortune, especially when it brings success, safety or an advantage
senses.definitionCN: 尤指带来成功、平安或优势的好运气
senses.example: It was pure luck that the last seat went to her.
senses.exampleCN: 最后那个座位落到她手里，纯属好运。
senses.why: Because people most often speak of luck when things turn out well, the neutral force narrowed into the favourable sense that dominates everyday use.
senses.whyCN: 因为人们通常在事情顺利时才提起 luck，这个中性的力量就收窄成日常最常用的「好运气」义。

senses.title: Success that comes by chance rather than skill
senses.definition: a favourable result that happened by accident rather than through skill or planning
senses.definitionCN: 凭偶然而非技巧或计划取得的有利结果
senses.example: The team won by luck rather than by better play.
senses.exampleCN: 这支队伍是靠侥幸而不是靠更好的发挥赢的。
senses.why: If good fortune can deliver a result, then a result delivered that way is itself called luck, so the cause and the outcome share one word.
senses.whyCN: 如果好运能带来结果，那么以这种方式得到的结果本身也被叫作 luck，于是原因与结果共用同一个词。

senses.title: One's personal fortune at a particular time
senses.definition: the state of a person's fortune at a given moment, which can rise or fall
senses.definitionCN: 一个人在某一时刻的运气状态，可升可降
senses.example: His luck changed the moment the manager noticed his work.
senses.exampleCN: 经理注意到他的工作那一刻，他的运势就变了。
senses.why: Luck as a force can also be treated as something a person possesses, so English speaks of someone's luck rising, falling or running out.
senses.whyCN: 作为力量的 luck 也可以被看成一个人所拥有的东西，于是英语会说某人的运气上升、下降或用完。

intro.en: Luck enters English in the fifteenth century from a Germanic source; its exact path is uncertain, but gambling gave it a firm place in everyday speech.
intro.cn: luck 于十五世纪从日耳曼语来源进入英语；确切路径不确定，但赌博让它在日常语言中站稳了脚。

items.en: Luck appears in written English in the fifteenth century as lucke, meaning good fortune.
items.cn: luck 在十五世纪以 lucke 的形式出现在书面英语中，意为好运。

items.en: Most accounts link it to Middle Dutch luc or the related Low German gelucke, though the exact path is not certain.
items.cn: 多数说法把它与中古荷兰语 luc 或相关的低地德语 gelucke 联系起来，但确切来源路径并不确定。

items.en: In the sixteenth century the word was common at dice and card tables, where fortune was visibly decided by chance.
items.cn: 十六世纪时这个词常用于骰子和牌桌，在那里运气明显由偶然决定。

items.en: From games it widened to any event that people believed chance had decided.
items.cn: 它从游戏扩展到人们认为由偶然决定的任何事情。

items.en: Modern English uses luck for chance as a force, for good fortune, and for success that came without skill.
items.cn: 现代英语用 luck 指作为力量的偶然、好运气，以及不靠技巧而得来的成功。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the luck family and a spelling neighbour; the near-meaning group collects words for chance and for what fortune brings.
note.cn: 形近组收 luck 词族与一个拼写相近的词；近义组收表示偶然以及命运所带来之物的词。

entries.definition: Having good fortune; built from luck with -y.
entries.definitionCN: 有好运的；由 luck 加 -y 构成。

entries.definition: By good fortune; fortunately.
entries.definitionCN: 幸运地；幸好。

entries.definition: Without good fortune, and often unfortunate.
entries.definitionCN: 运气不好的，常指倒霉。

entries.definition: A small case worn on a chain; only the spelling is close, and the origin is different.
entries.definitionCN: 挂在链上的小盒；只是拼写与 luck 相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: Chance or the good and bad things it brings.
entries.definitionCN: 偶然，以及它带来的好坏遭遇。

entries.definition: The possibility that something will happen, or events without a plan.
entries.definitionCN: 某事发生的可能性，或没有计划的事件。

entries.definition: The power believed to fix what will happen to a person.
entries.definitionCN: 被认为决定一个人遭遇的力量；命运。

entries.definition: A person's future seen as already settled.
entries.definitionCN: 被视为早已定下的人生归宿。

entries.definition: Bad luck or an unlucky event.
entries.definitionCN: 坏运气或不幸的事件。

normalIntro.en: The word is short and its origin uncertain, so the hooks come from its family, its fixed phrases and its long association with games of chance.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词很短，来源又不确定，所以记忆钩子来自它的词族、固定短语，以及它与碰运气游戏的长期联系。

normal.en: Lucky is luck plus -y, so the adjective simply means full of luck.
normal.cn: lucky 是 luck 加 -y，所以这个形容词的意思就是「带着运气的」。

normal.en: Luckily changes the y of lucky to i before adding -ly.
normal.cn: luckily 是先把 lucky 的 y 变成 i，再加 -ly。

normal.en: Luckless adds -less, the suffix of absence, so it means without luck.
normal.cn: luckless 加的是表示「没有」的后缀 -less，因此意为没有运气。

normal.en: By luck is a fixed phrase for something that happened through chance rather than plan.
normal.cn: by luck 是固定短语，指事情靠偶然而非计划发生。

normal.en: Luck out is informal and means to succeed by chance, keeping the old gambling flavour.
normal.cn: luck out 是口语说法，意为碰巧成功，保留了旧日赌博的意味。

abstract.en: A word for an unexplained cause becomes a word for a personal possession, because people would rather own fortune than admit they cannot explain it.
abstract.cn: 一个指无法解释之原因的词，变成了指个人所有物的词，因为人宁愿把运气归为己有，也不愿承认自己解释不了。

abstract.en: Luck sits between chance and fate: less planned than fate, more personal than pure chance.
abstract.cn: luck 处在偶然与命运之间：比命运更少安排，比纯粹的偶然更带个人色彩。

abstract.en: Every wish of good luck admits the same thing: the outcome is not fully in our hands.
abstract.cn: 每一句祝好运都承认同一件事：结果并不完全掌握在我们手里。

examples.en: It was pure luck that the last seat went to her.
examples.cn: 最后那个座位落到她手里，纯属好运。

examples.en: The team won by luck rather than by better play.
examples.cn: 这支队伍是靠侥幸而不是靠更好的发挥赢的。

examples.en: His luck changed the moment the manager noticed his work.
examples.cn: 经理注意到他的工作那一刻，他的运势就变了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「拉壳」——抽奖时一拉就开出好壳，记住 luck 是运气。

root: 来源不确定；一般认为与中古荷兰语 luc 或低地德语 gelucke 有关，十五世纪进入英语时意为好运；没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is chance as an unnamed force; the senses narrow into good fortune, then into success by accident and a person's shifting fortune.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是把偶然看作一种无名的力量；义项收窄为好运气，再分为意外得来的成功与个人起伏的运势。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a coin spinning in the air and landing upright on a fingertip, trembling but not falling.
core.cn: 核心意象：一枚硬币在空中翻转，落下时立在上方不稳，却始终没有倒下。

branches.en: a storm that turns aside for no clear reason
branches.cn: 毫无缘由地转向的风暴

branches.en: the last ticket going to the person who arrived late
branches.cn: 最后一张票落到迟到者手里

branches.en: a coin landing the right way at a card table
branches.cn: 牌桌上硬币恰好落在对的一面

branches.en: a weak side winning without doing anything clever
branches.cn: 弱队没使出什么高招却赢了

branches.en: a worker noticed just as his fortunes turn
branches.cn: 正逢运势转折时被注意到的工人

intro.en: Luck is a short Germanic noun, and English builds its family with two suffixes that mark presence and absence of fortune.
intro.cn: luck 是一个简短的日耳曼语名词，英语用两个后缀分别表示「有运气」与「没有运气」，撑起整个词族。

latinIntro.en: Luck comes from a Germanic source of uncertain path, so no reliable Latin cognate is recorded for it.
latinIntro.cn: luck 来自路径不确定的日耳曼语来源，因此没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.example: Luck played a part in the rescue.
items.exampleCN: 运气在救援中起了作用。

items.example: She was lucky to catch the last train.
items.exampleCN: 她赶上了末班车，真幸运。

items.example: Luckily, the rain stopped before the match.
The luckless traveller missed every connection.
items.exampleCN: 这位倒霉的旅客错过了每一次转乘。

items.meaningCN: 形容词后缀：由名词构成形容词
items.example: Luck plus -y gives lucky.
Luckless means without luck.
Luckily adds -ly to lucky.
items.exampleCN: luckily 是在 lucky 后加 -ly。

items.example: She found the letter by luck.

definition_zh: 幸运的；走运的；带来好运的；吉利的；侥幸的
definition_en: having good fortune; bringing good fortune; happening by chance in a favourable way; or believed to be auspicious
core_image: 一个人从口袋里摸出一张旧彩票，对着光一看，号码正好全部对上
scene: 雨刚停，一个赶路的人随手招了一下，空荡荡的街口竟真的停下一辆出租车。He felt lucky as the taxi pulled up beside him.
sceneCN: 这里 lucky 是「幸运的、走运的」（第 1 个义项：本人有好运）；句意为出租车在他身边停下时，他感到自己很走运。画面里可认出雨后的街口与停下的出租车。

pos.zh: 幸运的；走运的；带来好运的；吉利的；侥幸的

collocations.zh: 难得的好机会；意外的好运

derivatives.zh: 由 lucky 变 y 为 i 再加 -ly 构成，义为「幸运地；幸好」
由 lucky 加否定前缀 un- 构成，义为「不幸的；不吉利的」
由 lucky 加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「幸运」

senses.title: Having good fortune in a particular situation
senses.definition: enjoying good fortune, especially when something good happens by chance
senses.definitionCN: 享有好运，尤指好事偶然落到自己头上
senses.example: She felt lucky when the last ticket was still available.
senses.exampleCN: 最后一张票还没卖掉，她觉得自己很幸运。
senses.why: The noun luck names the force, and the suffix -y turns it into a quality, so a person can be described as having that force on their side.
senses.whyCN: 名词 luck 指这种力量，后缀 -y 把它变成一种性质，于是可以说一个人身上带着这种力量。

senses.title: Believed to bring good fortune to its owner
senses.definition: thought to bring good fortune to the person who has it or carries it
senses.definitionCN: 被认为能给拥有者或携带者带来好运的
senses.example: He wore the same shirt to every match because he believed it was lucky.
senses.exampleCN: 每逢比赛他都穿同一件衬衫，因为他相信那件衣服能带来好运。
senses.why: If a person can be lucky, then an object can be trusted to carry that luck, so the word spreads from people to charms and clothes.
senses.whyCN: 既然人可以走运，人们也会相信某件物品能承载这份运气，于是词义从人扩展到护身符和衣物。

senses.title: Happening by chance in a favourable way
senses.definition: favourable but produced by accident rather than by skill or knowledge
senses.definitionCN: 结果有利，却出自偶然而非技巧或知识
senses.example: It was a lucky guess, not real knowledge.
senses.exampleCN: 那只是侥幸猜中，并不是真懂。
senses.why: When a good result arrives without skill, English calls it lucky, because the outcome is credited to fortune rather than to the person.
senses.whyCN: 当好结果并非来自技巧时，英语称其为 lucky，因为这个结果被归功于运气而不是归功于人。

senses.title: Considered auspicious for a particular purpose
senses.definition: believed to be a favourable time, number or sign for something
senses.definitionCN: 被认为对某件事有利的时间、数字或征兆
senses.example: They chose the date because it was a lucky day in the old calendar.
senses.exampleCN: 他们选这个日期，是因为它在旧历里是幸运日。
senses.why: From charms the word extends to days, numbers and signs, because people look for fortune not only in objects but also in timing.
senses.whyCN: 从护身符出发，这个词又扩展到日子、数字与征兆，因为人们不只在物件里找运气，也在时机里找。

intro.en: Lucky is the noun luck with the adjective suffix -y; the noun itself came into English from a Germanic source whose exact path is uncertain.
intro.cn: lucky 是名词 luck 加形容词后缀 -y；这个名词本身来自日耳曼语来源，确切路径不确定。

items.en: Luck enters English in the fifteenth century, and the adjective lucky follows by adding -y to the noun.
items.cn: luck 于十五世纪进入英语，形容词 lucky 由名词加 -y 随后产生。

items.en: The noun is generally linked to Middle Dutch luc or Low German gelucke, though the exact source remains uncertain.
items.cn: 这个名词一般认为与中古荷兰语 luc 或低地德语 gelucke 有关，确切来源仍不确定。

items.en: Lucky appears in the sixteenth century, first around games of chance and then in ordinary speech.
items.cn: lucky 在十六世纪出现，最初用于碰运气的游戏，后来进入日常语言。

items.en: The suffix -y turns nouns into adjectives, as it does in health to healthy and luck to lucky.
items.cn: 后缀 -y 把名词变成形容词，health 变 healthy、luck 变 lucky 都是这样。

items.en: Modern English uses lucky for people, charms, guesses, breaks and auspicious days.
items.cn: 现代英语用 lucky 形容人、护身符、猜测、好机会与吉日。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the luck family and a word that merely rhymes; the near-meaning group collects adjectives for good fortune and its opposite.
note.cn: 形近组收 luck 词族与一个只是押韵的词；近义组收表示好运及其反面的形容词。

entries.definition: The noun behind lucky, meaning chance or good fortune.
entries.definitionCN: lucky 背后的名词，意为运气或好运。

entries.definition: By good fortune; the adverb built from lucky.
entries.definitionCN: 幸运地；由 lucky 构成的副词。

entries.definition: Having bad fortune; lucky with the negative prefix un-.
entries.definitionCN: 运气不好的；lucky 加否定前缀 un-。

entries.definition: Brave in a difficult situation; only the ending is close, and the root is different.
entries.definitionCN: 在困境中勇敢的；只是词尾与 lucky 相近，词根不同。

entries.definition: Having good fortune, often in a formal tone.
entries.definitionCN: 有好运的，语气常较正式。

entries.definition: Enjoying good fortune that is seen as a gift.
entries.definitionCN: 享有被视为恩赐的好运。

entries.definition: Given special help, advantage or preference.
entries.definitionCN: 得到特别帮助、优势或偏爱的。

entries.definition: Protected as if by magic; often a light or ironic word.
entries.definitionCN: 像受魔法保护般的；常带轻松或反讽语气。

entries.definition: Marked by bad fortune from the start.
entries.definitionCN: 从一开始就注定倒霉的。

normalIntro.en: The word is a transparent suffix build from luck, so its hooks come from the noun, the -y suffix and the spelling changes in comparison.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词由 luck 加后缀清楚构成，记忆钩子来自名词、-y 后缀以及比较级中的拼写变化。

normal.en: Lucky is luck plus -y, so the adjective means having or carrying luck.
normal.cn: lucky 是 luck 加 -y，所以这个形容词意为拥有或带着运气。

normal.en: The comparative is luckier: the final y becomes i before -er is added.
normal.cn: 比较级是 luckier：最后的 y 先变成 i，再加 -er。

normal.en: The superlative is luckiest, following the same y to i change.
normal.cn: 最高级是 luckiest，同样先把 y 变成 i。

normal.en: Unlucky adds the prefix un- to lucky and reverses the fortune.
normal.cn: unlucky 在 lucky 前加前缀 un-，把运气反过来。

normal.en: Lucky break and lucky charm are fixed phrases, one for a chance opportunity and one for a trusted object.
normal.cn: lucky break 与 lucky charm 是固定短语，一个指偶然得来的机会，一个指被信赖的物件。

abstract.en: Calling a shirt lucky shows how easily people move fortune out of the body and into an object they can control.
abstract.cn: 把一件衬衫说成幸运，说明人很容易把运气从身体转移到一件自己能控制的物品上。

abstract.en: A lucky guess is praised and distrusted at once, because we want the result but not the randomness behind it.
abstract.cn: 侥幸猜中同时得到赞许与怀疑，因为我们想要结果，却不喜欢结果背后的偶然。

abstract.en: A lucky day is a way of making time itself take sides with a plan.
abstract.cn: 吉日是一种让时间本身站在计划一边的说法。

examples.en: She felt lucky when the last ticket was still available.
examples.cn: 最后一张票还没卖掉，她觉得自己很幸运。

examples.en: He wore the same shirt to every match because he believed it was lucky.
examples.cn: 每逢比赛他都穿同一件衬衫，因为他相信那件衣服能带来好运。

examples.en: It was a lucky guess, not real knowledge.
examples.cn: 那只是侥幸猜中，并不是真懂。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「拉齐」——队伍拉得齐，运气自然来，记住 lucky 是幸运的。

root: luck（来源不确定，一般认为与中古荷兰语 luc 有关）加形容词后缀 -y；比较级把 y 变 i 再加 -er，写作 luckier。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is having good fortune; the senses spread to objects that carry luck, results that come by accident and times believed to be auspicious.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是本人拥有好运；义项扩展到承载运气的物件、偶然得来的结果，以及被认为吉利的时机。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand pulling an old ticket from a pocket and finding every number matches.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手从口袋里摸出一张旧彩票，发现号码全部对上。

branches.en: a traveller who finds the last taxi in the rain
branches.cn: 雨中赶上最后一辆出租车的行人

branches.en: a shirt worn again for every important match
branches.cn: 每场重要比赛都重穿的那件衬衫

branches.en: a small charm kept in a coat pocket
branches.cn: 放在外套口袋里的护身符

branches.en: an answer that turns out right for no clear reason
branches.cn: 说不出理由却恰好正确的答案

branches.en: a date chosen because the old calendar favours it
branches.cn: 因旧历相宜而选定的日期

intro.en: Lucky is the noun luck dressed with -y, and its family adds comparison, a negative prefix and a noun suffix.
intro.cn: lucky 是名词 luck 加 -y 构成，它的词族又加上比较级、否定前缀与名词后缀。

latinIntro.en: Lucky is a Germanic noun plus an English suffix, so it has no reliable Latin cognate.
latinIntro.cn: lucky 是日耳曼语名词加英语后缀构成，因此没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

items.example: Luck helped them find the road again.
items.exampleCN: 运气帮他们重新找到了路。

items.example: They were lucky to escape the storm.
items.exampleCN: 他们躲过风暴，真是幸运。

items.example: This year has been luckier than the last.
That was the luckiest day of his life.
items.exampleCN: 那是他一生中最幸运的一天。

items.example: Luckily, nobody was hurt.
Some actors think the play is unlucky.
items.exampleCN: 有些演员认为这部剧不吉利。

items.meaningCN: 形容词后缀：由名词构成形容词
items.example: Luck plus -y gives lucky.
Luckiness adds -ness to lucky.

definition_zh: 幸运地；侥幸地；幸好；好在
definition_en: by good chance; fortunately, especially because something bad was avoided
core_image: 躲过一劫后长出一口气：刚才差一点就出事
scene: 差一步就要踩到积水的台阶，好在突然停住了脚步。I had already stepped out, but luckily there was a rail to catch.
sceneCN: 说话人差一点摔倒，最后抓住栏杆躲过一劫——这里 luckily 表示「幸好、侥幸躲过」（第 1 个义项：事情的结果偏向幸运一面）。

pos.zh: 幸运地；幸好（修饰整个句子）

derivatives.zh: 运气；幸运，luckily 的名词基础
幸运的；吉利的，luck 加形容词后缀 -y 而来
幸运；好运，形容词再加名词后缀 -ness

senses.title: Happening by good fortune
senses.definition: used to say that something good happened because of chance, not because anyone planned it
senses.definitionCN: 指某件好事因偶然机会发生，并非事先安排所致
senses.example: Luckily, the train was delayed, so we did not miss it.
senses.exampleCN: 幸好火车晚点了，我们才没错过。
senses.why: The adverb grows straight out of the noun luck: when luck works in your favor, the whole outcome turns out well.
senses.whyCN: 副词直接从名词 luck 长出来：运气站在你这一边，整个结果就朝好的方向发展。

senses.title: Escaping a bad result narrowly
senses.definition: used when something bad almost happened but was avoided by chance
senses.definitionCN: 指坏事几乎发生，却因偶然因素得以避免
senses.example: He fell off the ladder but luckily landed on a pile of leaves.
senses.exampleCN: 他从梯子上摔下来，但侥幸落在一堆树叶上。
senses.why: The core image is the near miss: luck intervenes at the last moment so the danger stays unreal.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是「差一点出事」：运气在最后一刻介入，危险始终没有成真。

senses.title: Adding a grateful comment to a statement
senses.definition: used at the start of a sentence to show relief that a situation was not worse
senses.definitionCN: 置于句首，表示庆幸情况没有更糟
senses.example: Luckily for us, the shop still had one ticket left.
senses.exampleCN: 对我们来说幸运的是，商店还剩一张票。
senses.why: English often turns adverbs into sentence-level comments; luckily works like fortunately to color the whole clause.
senses.whyCN: 英语常把副词用作整句的评注；luckily 和 fortunately 一样为整个句子染上庆幸的语气。

intro.en: Luckily is a young English adverb built directly on the noun luck, a word with northern Germanic roots.
intro.cn: luckily 是一个较年轻的英语副词，直接建立在名词 luck 之上，而 luck 源自北部日耳曼语。

items.en: The noun luck is generally traced to Old Norse happ, later a personal name Lukka, meaning chance or good fortune.
items.cn: 名词 luck 一般追溯到古诺斯语 happ（后作人名 Lukka），意为机会或好运。

items.en: Northern Dutch and Low German kept related forms such as luk, which helped carry the word into northern English speech.
items.cn: 荷兰北部与低地德语保留了 luk 等相关形式，帮助该词进入英格兰北部口语。

items.en: In Middle English luck meant fortune or chance, especially good fortune, and spread from the north to the whole country.
items.cn: 中古英语中 luck 意为运气或机会，尤指好运，并从北方扩散到全国。

items.en: The wider Germanic family links luck with words for happiness, since happ is also the source of happy.
items.cn: 更广的日耳曼语族把 luck 与「幸福」类词汇联系起来，因为 happ 同时也是 happy 的来源。

items.en: The adverb luckily formed in Modern English as luck plus the adverbial suffix -ly, first recorded in the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 现代英语中 luckily 由 luck 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，最早见于十六世纪。

note.en: These neighbors either share luck as a base or compete with luckily in meaning.
note.cn: 这些邻近词要么共享词根 luck，要么在意义上与 luckily 相互竞争。

entries.definition: the noun that luckily is built from; good or bad fortune
entries.definitionCN: luckily 的构词基础；好或坏的运气

entries.definition: adjective form of luck; having good fortune
entries.definitionCN: luck 的形容词形式；幸运的

entries.definition: the state of being lucky
entries.definitionCN: 幸运的状态；好运的属性

entries.definition: very close synonym; it happened by good fortune
entries.definitionCN: 与 luckily 最接近的同义词；事情因好运发生

entries.definition: can mean by good chance, but also means joyfully
entries.definitionCN: 可指侥幸，也可指快乐地，语义更宽

entries.definition: idiom meaning by chance, for better or worse
entries.definitionCN: 习语：碰巧（可指好运也可指坏运）

normalIntro.en: Five ways to anchor luckily through its family and grammar.
normalIntro.cn: 从词族和语法两个角度记住 luckily 的五条线索。

normal.en: luck + -ly: turn the noun luck into an adverb.
normal.cn: luck 加副词后缀 -ly：把名词「运气」变成副词。

normal.en: lucky is the adjective pair; luckily is its adverb twin.
normal.cn: lucky 是形容词搭档，luckily 是它的副词孪生兄弟。

normal.en: Sentence adverb: luckily can stand at the front with a comma.
normal.cn: 作句首副词：luckily 可放在句首并用逗号隔开。

normal.en: Compare happily: luck and happ both mean good chance.
normal.cn: 对照 happily：luck 与 happ（幸福）本是同源意象。

normal.en: Frequently tells how often; luckily tells how the dice fell.
normal.cn: frequently 说频率，luckily 说骰子掷出的结果。

abstract.en: Picture a coin landing heads at the exact second you needed it.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚硬币恰好在最需要的时刻正面朝上落地。

abstract.en: See a falling plate caught just before it hits the floor.
abstract.cn: 看见一个盘子坠向地面、在摔碎前一秒被接住。

abstract.en: Feel the relief in one long breath after the danger passes.
abstract.cn: 危险过后长长舒一口气的庆幸感。

examples.en: Luckily, the fire alarm rang before the smoke spread.
examples.cn: 幸好火警在烟雾蔓延前就响了。

examples.en: She had no umbrella, but luckily a stranger offered to share his.
examples.cn: 她没带伞，但幸好一位陌生人愿意与他共用。

examples.en: He guessed the last answer, and it turned out to be right.
examples.cn: 他猜了最后一道题的答案，结果竟然对了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「拉起利」——运气把人从坑里拉起来，自然有利：拉起来就幸运了。

root: luck 是英语北源的日耳曼词，一般认为借自古诺斯语 happ（机会、好运，亦为 happy 的来源），经低地德语区口语进入中古英语；luckily 在现代英语期加上副词后缀 -ly 构成。

sensesIntro.en: From plain good luck to narrow escapes and a grateful sentence comment.
sensesIntro.cn: 从单纯的好运，到惊险脱险，再到句首庆幸的语气词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a near miss that ends well
core.cn: 核心意象：差一点出事，结果却朝好的方向收场

branches.en: Good fortune makes the outcome positive.
branches.cn: 好运让结果转向好的一面。

branches.en: Danger almost lands but is dodged by chance.
branches.cn: 危险几乎落下来，却被偶然躲开。

branches.en: The speaker adds relief as a comment on the whole sentence.
branches.cn: 说话人把庆幸作为对整句的评注。

branches.en: Both senses rest on chance, not planning.
branches.cn: 两个义项都建立在偶然而非计划之上。

branches.en: A narrow escape naturally triggers the feeling of relief.
branches.cn: 惊险脱险自然引出庆幸之情。

intro.en: Luckily is built with a simple adverbial suffix on a Germanic noun base.
intro.cn: luckily 由日耳曼名词加简单副词后缀构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin has no direct role here, but parallel adverbs show the same pattern.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语在此并无直接参与，但平行的副词构造展现了相同模式。

items.meaning: in the manner of; turns adjectives into adverbs
items.meaningCN: 以……方式；把形容词变为副词
items.example: quickly means in a quick manner.
items.exampleCN: quickly 意为「以快速的方式」。

items.example: Luck was on our side today.
items.exampleCN: 今天运气站在我们这边。

items.structure: cognate from the same Norse root
items.example: The happy ending surprised no one.
items.exampleCN: 圆满结局没让任何人意外。

items.example: Fortunately, nobody was hurt.
Unluckily, the bus had just left.

items.structure: kin noun from the same Norse root
items.example: A slight mishap delayed the start.
items.exampleCN: 一点小事故让开始时间推迟了。

items.example: Haply you will find it there.
items.exampleCN: 或许你能在那里找到它。

items.example: Perhaps the rain will stop soon.
